text_blocks.snippet: Scams across Central Illinois are on the rise, with fraudsters increasingly utilizing phone spoofing, artificial intelligence (AI), fake text messages, and imposter tactics to target residents.
snippet_highlighted_words: phone spoofing, artificial intelligence (AI), fake text messages, and imposter tactics

list.snippet: Bank Imposter & Phone Spoofing Scams: Scammers are spoofing phone numbers—including those of local banks (such as Fisher National Bank and Federated Bank) and federal or local law enforcement—to make calls look legitimate on caller ID. They claim you have missed jury duty, face a license suspension, or are the subject of a criminal/sex trafficking investigation, demanding immediate payment or financial details.

AI-Generated Voice & Romance Scams: Law enforcement agencies like the Peoria County Sheriff's Office warn that AI-generated voice cloning is being used to make fake emergency or romance scams sound real. Scammers build online connections before requesting money or sensitive data.

State Agency & Secretary of State Phishing: Fraudsters are sending mass texts, emails, and calls impersonating state departments (including the Illinois Secretary of State) threatening driving privilege revocations or demanding unpaid ticket fees.

Home Repair & Storm Chaser Scams: Door-to-door solicitors and temporary contractors offer quick or "free" storm damage inspections, demanding large cash advances or upfront full payments without proper licensing.

Hang up and verify: Legitimate banks, courts, and state agencies will never call or text demanding immediate payment, login credentials, or sensitive personal data over the phone. Hang up and dial the official number listed on your bank statement, card, or government website.
Do not click links: Never click links in unsolicited text messages or emails claiming to be from state offices or delivery services.
Check local warnings: Stay updated on regional advisories through resources like the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois or local bank alerts highlighted via Fox 2 Now.
Report fraud: Report suspicious activity to the Illinois Attorney General’s Consumer Fraud Bureau, the Better Business Bureau, or your local county sheriff's office.

text_blocks.snippet: If you received a specific suspicious call, text, or visit, tell me what they claimed so I can help you figure out if it is a known scam.
